subject.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall

question: Should OpenClaw accept SourceActor as the public plugin/message/memory attribution contract for this stack, or should the contract be renamed, narrowed, or delayed before release?
rationale: The code path is mechanically plausible, but the PR creates public plugin-facing fields and carries participant metadata into prompt and memory surfaces; automation cannot choose the long-term API and privacy boundary.

options.title: Approve SourceActor Contract
options.body: Treat this PR as the memory follow-up after the prerequisite Signal/source-actor stack lands, with SourceActor/sourceActor as the accepted public attribution vocabulary.

options.title: Rename Or Narrow Before Release
options.body: Ask for a smaller or differently named API surface if maintainers want fewer scalar mirrors, less participant metadata, or different trust wording.

options.title: Pause The Stack
options.body: Keep the PR draft or close later if maintainers decide participant attribution should be structurally stored before exposing best-effort memory context.

recommendation.title: Approve SourceActor Contract
recommendation.body: Treat this PR as the memory follow-up after the prerequisite Signal/source-actor stack lands, with SourceActor/sourceActor as the accepted public attribution vocabulary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing history spans the inbound context, plugin tool context, memory, and Signal surfaces that define this public contract.
